source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    To check setting dedicated port as DHCP for ipv4 is normal.
1. Plug network cable on dedicated  and chcek the link status
2. Power on system and boot into BIOS setup
3. Goto "server mgmt" page to check BMC ip
4. Check the ip source is on DHCP mode
5. Use this to login BMC Web

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Check the ip can be present on BIOS
2. Check the Web can be login

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Set dedicated port as DHCP(IPv4) (Dedicated as DHCP IPv4): agent reads the BMC LAN source/address with ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address|Subnet|DHCP|Source" (or Redfish EthernetInterface read via curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/1/EthernetInterfaces" 2>&1); setting the DHCP mode itself is done in BMC/BIOS UI by the operator.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the lan-print/Redfish IPv4 address-source output so the user confirms the Dedicated port is on DHCP(IPv4) and the IP is present; the mode change + web-login are operator/UI steps.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: enabling DHCP may drop the operator's static management IP; confirm the console path before toggling.

original_test_intent: Verify that the dedicated BMC management port operates in IPv4 DHCP mode, obtains an address visible in BIOS Server Management and permits login to the BMC WebUI at the assigned address.
original_method: An engineer connects the dedicated cable, boots to BIOS, confirms the DHCP source and assigned IPv4 address on the Server Management page, then performs a BMC WebUI login using that address.
manual_activity: The source requires physical cabling, BIOS page inspection and BMC WebUI login. Those UI observations are core acceptance activities, even though readback of the resulting DHCP configuration can be automated.
required_inputs: Approved DHCP server, VLAN, lease range/reservation, routes and address-discovery method
Current BMC network configuration and exact rollback values
BMC credentials, console/KVM access and maintenance authorization
safety_requirements: Do not enable DHCP on an unmapped BMC channel or without verified lease discovery.
Retain an independent console/OOB path because the current static address may immediately stop responding.
Protect credentials; avoid password command-line arguments and do not disable TLS verification in a formal method without an approved trust exception.
Stop on no lease, duplicate address, wrong VLAN or management loss; preserve state and do not retry automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Capture the mapped channel's pre/post address source, MAC, IPv4 settings and BMC health using an approved read-only interface.
Correlate the DHCP lease with operator BIOS and WebUI evidence and organize logs.
Verify final approved reachability without deciding the formal result.
engineer_actions: Approve the management-IP transition and rollback plan.
Perform cabling, BIOS DHCP/source/address inspection and BMC WebUI login.
Assess the UI and network evidence and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The readback is supporting evidence only. Channel 1, Manager 1 and EthernetInterface paths must be discovered for the platform, and `-P`/inline basic credentials plus `-k` are unsuitable defaults for formal evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After mapping, use the vendor-supported read-only Redfish/IPMI endpoint with protected credentials and full unfiltered output to confirm DHCP source, lease address and MAC.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Dedicated cabling, power-on, BIOS DHCP/IP display, WebUI login and 5/0-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: RETAIN BIOS/WEBUI METHOD WITH SAFE READBACK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Archive the existing static configuration, verify console recovery and DHCP lease discovery, have the engineer enable/confirm DHCP through the source-approved UI path, then correlate BIOS, lease, API readback and authenticated WebUI evidence.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Mapped BMC channel and approved IPv4 DHCP segment.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/BIOS firmware, API/tool version and DHCP server configuration revision.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BMC network guide and project DHCP/VLAN plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds pre-change recovery, lease correlation and secure readback without replacing BIOS/WebUI acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; an old-address `lan print` alone is insufficient.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: DHCP scope, mapping, discovery and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The management address can change before remote tooling reconnects.

project_override_considerations: The project supplies its DHCP scope, reservation and approved final state. A project may keep DHCP enabled afterward or restore the prior state as approved. Missing project parameters are readiness gaps, not permanent BLOCKED; API-only validation changes the explicit UI coverage.
expected_evidence: Pre-change mapped channel/MAC, configuration and approved DHCP/rollback plan
Lease record plus BIOS screenshots showing DHCP source and assigned IPv4
Successful authenticated BMC WebUI login at the assigned address
Final reachability, post-change readback/log review and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item, procedure and criteria consistently describe DHCP assignment, BIOS address visibility and BMC WebUI access on the dedicated port.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation is clear. Missing project DHCP/network values prevent execution readiness but do not create a permanent semantic block.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retain its readback and lockout warning, but reject PARTIAL under the locked manual WebUI/BIOS acceptance rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain its detailed DHCP and rollback requirements while reclassifying the core UI-driven case as MANUAL ONLY.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates automated configuration evidence from the engineer-performed BIOS/WebUI acceptance and formal verdict.

review_improvement: Adds lease-to-MAC correlation and a pre-recorded rollback path so a stale or wrong BMC address cannot be mistaken for successful DHCP operation.
independent_technical_reasoning: The DHCP state can be read electronically, but the source's two formal criteria are presentation in BIOS and login through BMC WebUI. Because both are human-observed core steps, the locked V3.1 classification is MANUAL ONLY rather than PARTIAL.
